title: MAHARASHTRA CLASS 4 — English | Creative Writing
description: Subject-wise test on Creative Writing (English) for MAHARASHTRA CLASS 4. 25Q.
subject: maha4-english

questions.question: What is the correct expansion of the idiom in the sentence: 'When the teacher announced surprise tests, all students had to ______.'

options.text: turn a blind eye
options.explanation: This idiom means to ignore something deliberately, which does not fit the context.

options.text: bite the bullet
options.explanation: Correct idiom meaning to face a difficult situation bravely.

options.text: let the cat out of the bag
options.explanation: This idiom means to reveal a secret, which is unrelated to the context.

options.text: hit the sack
options.explanation: This idiom means to go to bed, which does not fit the context.

questions.explanation: The idiom 'bite the bullet' means to face a difficult situation bravely. In the context of surprise tests, students must endure the challenge without complaining.
questions.hint: Think about facing a tough situation without complaining.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct format for writing an informal letter to a friend?

options.text: Dear Sir, … Yours faithfully,
options.explanation: This format is used for formal letters, not informal ones.

options.text: Dear Friend, … Yours lovingly
options.explanation: Correct format for an informal letter to a friend.

options.text: To, The Principal, … Yours obediently
options.explanation: This format is used for formal letters to authorities.

options.text: Respected Teacher, … With regards
options.explanation: This format is used for formal letters to teachers.

questions.explanation: Informal letters use friendly salutations like 'Dear Friend' and closings like 'Yours lovingly.' Other options are either too formal or incorrect.
questions.hint: Informal letters are written to friends, so the tone should be friendly.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: Which sentence best describes the picture of a child planting a sapling with a smiling adult watching?

options.text: The child is crying while planting a tree.
options.explanation: The image shows a happy child, not a crying one.

options.text: The child is planting a sapling with the help of an adult, and both are happy.
options.explanation: This sentence accurately describes the activity and emotions in the image.

options.text: The adult is watering the plants alone.
options.explanation: The image shows both the child and the adult involved in planting.

options.text: The child is holding a broken pot.
options.explanation: The image does not show a broken pot or any such activity.

questions.explanation: The correct sentence matches the image by accurately describing the activity and emotions shown.
questions.hint: Look for a sentence that mentions both the child and the adult, and their emotions.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: In a diary entry about 'A day I will never forget,' which sentence shows the correct use of past tense and personal reflection?

options.text: I go to the beach with my family.
options.explanation: This sentence is in the present tense, not suitable for a diary entry.

options.text: I am feeling very excited about the trip.
options.explanation: This sentence is in the present tense and does not reflect a past experience.

options.text: I went to the beach with my family and felt so happy.
options.explanation: This sentence uses past tense and reflects a personal experience.

options.text: I will go to the beach tomorrow with my family.
options.explanation: This sentence is in the future tense, not suitable for a diary entry.

questions.explanation: Diary entries are written in the past tense and reflect personal experiences, as shown in option C.
questions.hint: Look for a sentence that uses past tense and expresses personal feelings.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a correct step in writing a paragraph?

options.text: Start with a topic sentence that introduces the main idea.
options.explanation: This is a correct step in writing a paragraph.

options.text: Use at least three supporting sentences with details.
options.explanation: This is a correct step in writing a paragraph.

options.text: End with a conclusion sentence that summarizes the paragraph.
options.explanation: This is a correct step in writing a paragraph.

options.text: Include dialogue between two characters in every paragraph.
options.explanation: Dialogue is not a required step in writing a paragraph.

questions.explanation: While dialogue can be included, it is not a required step in writing a paragraph. The other options are essential components.
questions.hint: Think about the basic structure of a paragraph.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: What is the correct message to leave for your mother when going to your friend’s house to play?

options.text: Mother, I am going to play at Ravi’s house. I will be back by 5 pm.
options.explanation: This message is clear, concise, and includes the necessary information.

options.text: Dear Mother, I have gone to play. Please come soon.
options.explanation: This message is too vague and does not include the time of return.

options.text: To my mother, I am playing outside. Don’t worry.
options.explanation: This message is too informal and lacks necessary details.

options.text: Mom, I went to a friend’s house. Call me when you return.
options.explanation: This message is in the past tense and does not inform about the current plan.

questions.explanation: The correct message is concise, includes the necessary information, and uses an informal tone suitable for a message to a family member.
questions.hint: Look for a message that is clear, concise, and includes the time of return.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: What is the correct expansion of the proverb: 'Too many cooks spoil the broth'?

options.text: This means that when too many people try to do the same thing, the result becomes messy or ruined.
options.explanation: Correct expansion of the proverb.

options.text: This means that cooking is a difficult task.
options.explanation: This is not the correct expansion of the proverb.

options.text: This means that broth is the best food to eat.
options.explanation: This is not the correct expansion of the proverb.

options.text: This means that chefs should always work together.
options.explanation: This is not the correct expansion of the proverb.

questions.explanation: The proverb means that too many people involved in something can lead to a poor outcome, as explained in option A.
questions.hint: Think about what happens when too many people try to do the same thing.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of a diary entry for a memorable day in school?

options.text: Today I woke up late and missed the bus.
options.explanation: This sentence does not reflect a memorable day in school.

options.text: On Monday, our class went on a picnic to the park. We played games and ate sandwiches. I felt so happy because it was my first time going there.
options.explanation: This sentence reflects a personal experience with emotions and details.

options.text: The picnic was nice, and the food was good.
options.explanation: This sentence lacks personal emotions and details.

options.text: I think picnics are better than regular classes.
options.explanation: This sentence is an opinion and does not reflect a personal experience.

questions.explanation: A diary entry should reflect a personal experience with emotions and details, as shown in option B.
questions.hint: Look for a sentence that includes personal emotions and details about the experience.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): In an informal letter, you should use simple and friendly language. Reason (R): The purpose of an informal letter is to communicate casually with friends or family.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are correct, and the reason explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is correct, and the reason correctly explains why informal language is used in informal letters.

questions.question: Which sentence should Rohan place FIRST in his paragraph to introduce the main idea?

options.text: Sentence 3
options.explanation: Sentence 3 describes the teacher's appearance, not the main idea.

options.text: Sentence 1
options.explanation: Sentence 1 introduces the main subject: Rohan's favorite teacher is Mrs. Sharma.

options.text: Sentence 5
options.explanation: Sentence 5 expresses Rohan's desire to become a teacher, which is not the main idea.

options.text: Sentence 2
options.explanation: Sentence 2 describes what the teacher teaches, not the main idea.

questions.explanation: The topic sentence of a paragraph should introduce the main subject. Sentence 1 clearly states the main idea: Rohan's favorite teacher is Mrs. Sharma.
questions.hint: Look for the sentence that introduces the main subject of the paragraph.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: Read the following sentences and choose the correct order to form a meaningful paragraph: (i) She wanted to share the joy with her friend. (ii) Neha saw a beautiful rainbow after the rain stopped. (iii) Neha decided to write a letter to her friend Priya. (iv) The sky was full of bright colors.

options.text: (ii), (iv), (iii), (i)
options.explanation: This is the correct order, but the question asks for the correct option, which is marked as C.

options.text: (iv), (ii), (i), (iii)
options.explanation: This order does not follow the logical sequence of events.

options.text: (ii), (iv), (iii), (i)
options.explanation: This is the correct order as it follows the sequence of events logically.

options.text: (iii), (ii), (iv), (i)
options.explanation: This order does not follow the logical sequence of events.

questions.explanation: The correct sequence begins with Neha seeing the rainbow (ii), then describing the sky (iv), deciding to write a letter (iii), and finally wanting to share the joy (i).
questions.hint: Start with the event that happens first and follow the logical flow of actions.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: In a diary entry describing a school picnic, which tense should be primarily used?

options.text: Future tense
options.explanation: Future tense is not used for events that have already happened.

options.text: Past tense
options.explanation: Past tense is used to describe events that have already occurred.

options.text: Present tense
options.explanation: Present tense is not used for past events.

options.text: Conditional tense
options.explanation: Conditional tense is not appropriate for diary entries.

questions.question: Choose the correct expansion for the idiom: 'A stitch in time saves nine.'

options.text: If you sew quickly, you can save nine stitches.
options.explanation: This is a literal interpretation, not the intended meaning of the idiom.

options.text: It is better to complete work early to avoid last-minute rush.
options.explanation: This is a close interpretation but not the exact meaning of the idiom.

options.text: Fixing a small problem early prevents it from becoming a bigger issue later.
options.explanation: This is the correct interpretation of the idiom.

options.text: Nine stitches are always needed to save time.
options.explanation: This is a literal and incorrect interpretation of the idiom.

questions.explanation: The idiom means that addressing a problem promptly prevents it from worsening.
questions.hint: Think about the meaning of 'stitch' and 'saves nine' in this context.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is the most suitable topic sentence for a paragraph about 'My Favorite Season'?

options.text: Winter is very cold.
options.explanation: This sentence is too general and does not introduce a personal preference.

options.text: Summer is my favorite season because I love swimming and eating ice cream.
options.explanation: This sentence introduces the main idea and provides a reason for the preference.

options.text: The trees are green in summer.
options.explanation: This sentence is too general and does not introduce a personal preference.

options.text: I like all seasons equally.
options.explanation: This sentence does not introduce a specific preference for a season.

questions.explanation: The topic sentence introduces the main idea and gives a reason for preference, which is ideal for a paragraph.
questions.hint: A topic sentence should introduce the main idea and provide a reason or detail.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: Read the following and choose the correct message format: You are leaving a note for your mother to inform her that you will be late for dinner because you are attending a school function.

options.text: Mother, I will be late for dinner. I am going to a friend's house.
options.explanation: This message does not mention the school function.

options.text: Mom, I’ll be home late today. There’s a school function, so don’t wait for me.
options.explanation: This message is concise, informal, and clearly conveys the necessary information.

options.text: Dear Mother, I am attending a function, so I will come back late for dinner.
options.explanation: This message is too formal for a note to a mother.

options.text: To Mom, I am busy with school work and will not have dinner.
options.explanation: This message does not mention the school function or the reason for being late.

questions.explanation: The message is concise, informal, and clearly conveys the necessary information in a friendly tone.
questions.hint: Consider the tone and clarity of the message.
questions.subject: maha4-english

questions.question: Which of the following diary entries uses the correct tone and tense?

options.text: I will go to the park tomorrow with my friends. It will be fun.
options.explanation: This entry uses future tense, which is not suitable for a diary entry.

options.text: Today, I went to the park with my friends. We played games and had a lot of fun.
options.explanation: This entry uses past tense and a personal tone, which is appropriate for a diary entry.

options.text: I go to the park every day with my friends. It is fun.
options.explanation: This entry uses present tense, which is not suitable for a diary entry.

questions.explanation: The diary entry uses past tense and a personal tone ('I went,' 'We played'), which is appropriate for diary writing.
questions.hint: Consider the tone and tense suitable for a diary entry.
